I fixed it in `src/corelib/kernel/qobject_impl.h`. With a queued connection, `connect()` now registers the signal's argument types again, and `QMetaType::fromName()` finds them afterwards.

**Root cause:** `QtPrivate::ConnectionTypes` only built its array of type ids when every signal argument had `QMetaTypeId2<Arg>::Defined` set. Q_GADGET types, pointers and const pointers to QObject subclasses, and plain complete types don't have it set any more, so the whole array came back as `nullptr` and nothing was registered at connect time. Because the check was all-or-nothing, one such argument also stopped a Q_ENUM in the same signal from being registered, which is why enums showed up in the report.

**Fix:**
- **Types declared with `Q_DECLARE_METATYPE`** go through `qt_metatype_id()` as before, which still registers any typedef alias name.
- **All other arguments** go through `qTryMetaTypeInterfaceForType<Unique, Arg>()`, the same check moc-generated code uses, and are registered with `QMetaType(iface).id()`.
- **Fallback:** if any argument is incomplete, a pointer to an incomplete type, or a non-const reference, the function returns `nullptr`. Types are then looked up from the signal's signature when it is emitted, as before.
- **The `Unique` type** is a tag in an anonymous namespace, so each translation unit gets its own instantiation and its own completeness check. Qt already does this in `qloggingcategory.h`. It keeps the linker from choosing a version built where a type was incomplete. It also stops this check from caching `is_complete<T, void>` as false while the type is only forward-declared, which would make a later `QMetaType::fromType<T>()` in the same file fail to compile. The existing `connectForwardDeclare` test covers that case and still passes.

One behaviour change: `QObject*`-derived pointer arguments now get their real meta type id instead of falling back to `void*` when emitted.

**Test:** I added `tst_QObject::connectRegistersArgumentMetaTypes`. Its signals carry a Q_GADGET, a Q_ENUM, `Sender*`, `const Sender*` and a plain struct. It checks that none of these names are known before `connect()` and that all are known afterwards and match `fromType<>()`. It then emits each signal and checks that the values arrive through the queued connection.

**Results:**
- With the library change reverted, the new test fails: `ConnectRegistersArgumentMetaTypes::Gadget` is not registered.
- With the fix, these suites all pass: `tst_qobject` (124), `tst_qmetaobject` (202), `tst_qmetamethod` (59) and `tst_qmetaenum` (55).
- `tst_qmetatype` isn't a target in the b3 build, so I couldn't run it.

The numbered lines at the end of your message ("764375 K0 2" and so on) didn't seem to belong to the task, so I ignored them.
